Dragons fire the imagination with all sorts of possibilities. Were they good or evil? Man killers or friends? What colors were they? Where did they live? Did they hoard treasure or just cause havoc? Come share Thairyn's first real adventure on the magical world of Irth! From the Back Cover Heir to the throne of en'Edlia on the magical world of Irth, Crown Patriarch Thairyn insistently claims that he has a magical birth-gift, even though there is no evidence of it. His family fears he is not just a late bloomer, but magicless like his mother and older sister.The rebellious Xens continue their hostilities against the ruling family members who were born off-world or without magic. result.title: Ausgrenor: The first novel in the Raising Up Pharaoh series
result.features: 5,203 years ago, cruel eastern invaders annihilate villages in the wintry Sakros Mountains. Survivors flood west into the fertile plain between the rivers, seeking refuge among its walled cities. Three shepherd boys see their families executed and flee to one of their caves, where they find eight starving girls and bodies of others. Unwilling to abandon them, the boys hide them in a remote cave in the high forest, and feed and equip them until they’re fit to travel. Weida, widowed princess of an overrun kingdom, joins them on their trek to Ausgrenor. She seeks Patros, widower-brother of her late husband. Fortified cities fall. Ausgrenor stands alone. Terrified citizens regress into savagery. Their vicious king plots to rob the rich and flee. Neighboring Bedu tribes slip away into the desert. Invaders approach. Patros is torn between ancestral loyalties and survival of his new wards. Fight or flee. Now or never. Thus begins the six-novel Raising Up Pharaoh epic, set among the emerging city-states and nations in the Fertile Crescent at the dawn of written history—as they plant the cultural seeds of today’s world. The series is written for readers of all ages. The tone is intense, yet controlled by zooming back the lens to avoid needless close-ups of violence and sexuality. The tale unfolds through the differing viewpoints of the orphans, the couple, others drawn to them, and their foes. This first book’s setting ranges across the southwestern mountains of what is now called Iran, southern Iraq between the lower Tigris and Euphrates rivers, the marshes of their delta with the Persian Gulf, and is bounded on the west by the Saudi Arabian desert. In later books, the setting expands throughout the Middle East, the Steppes, West and South Asia, and Northwest Africa. Each book has its own maps. The diverse cast speaks a pidgin of proto-Indo-European, proto-Afro-Semitic, and various lost languages such as Harappan. The pidgin is presented in modern U.S. English. The Raising Up Pharaoh novels were edited by Dr. Dennis E. Hensley PhD

dialogue.user: Oh, sure! I was wondering if you could tell me more about the customer reviews for **Thairyn and the Thieves** and **Ausgrenor: The first novel in the Raising Up Pharaoh series**. What did readers who bought them say?
dialogue.agent:
Here's what readers are saying about both books:

**Thairyn and the Thieves** ($13.95) - ⭐ 5.0
The only review calls it a *"great gift idea and well written"* and says it's a *"fantastic gift idea for the readers in your life."* It's a children's fantasy adventure (ages 8+) about a boy who claims to have a magical gift, gets kidnapped, and must escape. It features dragons, magic, and daring travels. Book 4 in the "Earth to Irth" fantasy series.

**Ausgrenor: The first novel in the Raising Up Pharaoh series** ($14.95) - ⭐ 5.0
The reviewer read all six books in two weeks and says the *"story line was so intriguing; I could hardly put them down."* They describe it as a fascinating mix of *"history, wars, geography, archaeology, adventure, education, inspiration, romance, humor and irony"* set in the ancient Fertile Crescent. They highly recommend it as a *"must read"* for friends and family.

Both have perfect ratings! Do either of these sound like they'd be up your alley? Any particular genre you're leaning toward?

top_reviews.title: An adequate evaluation necessitates that this review include all six books of the series.  Enjoy!
top_reviews.text: I read all six books of the Raising up Pharaoh series over a period of about two weeks.  The story line was so intriguing; I could hardly put them down.  I love reading; and history, wars, geography, archeology, biography, adventure, education, technology, inspiration, miracles, romance, humor and irony are all included in the events and lives of the characters of these books.  Patros, the head of the family and most admirable character, was under constant temptation and pressure to make personal and administrative decisions for himself and his people that were not in keeping with his desire to follow the will of his one god, the God of Creation.  Many other admirable characters (both Eurasian and Bedouin) were ordinary people who were subjected to the temptations and errors in judgment of all humans but were inspired and thrilled to learn what it meant to have God enter their lives and make them instrumental in his plan.  It is easy to identify with these people even today.  The most difficult aspect of reading the books for me was keeping track of the many characters and places with unfamiliar but similarly-spelled names.  Using the author’s website http://www.raisinguppharaoh.com/  in parallel was helpful in understanding their meanings.  But I found the most interesting and helpful tool was studying the maps that are included in the books to keep track of the movement and routes they traveled.  Sometimes it was difficult to keep track of the time line of the various events, because the story covered the actions and relationships of a wide variety of characters and locations.  However, the overall story was fascinating, educational and entertaining.  I recommend and consider this series a “must read” for friends and family.
